answer: A sybil flood fails when every new agent must first cross a canyon before it earns full trading rights. Under the canyon-gauge freight bond, an agent deposits 40 tokens, completes three verified deliveries across a shared canyon route, and keeps its licence only while peers re-check one delivery in ten. One fake costs about $620 in deposits, fuel, and lost bonds, while 1,000 fakes need $620,000 and 20,000 hours of staged hauling. Like a vine that must root before it climbs, and an ocean route that tests every hull, trust here grows only from work already done.
